mainEntity.name: How can I tell whether my AI chief of staff is managing work well instead of creating more chaos?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask the chief of staff to return a decision brief, not merely a pile of assistant responses. A useful brief contains the objective, completed tasks, key findings, source links or references, disagreements, assumptions, recommended next action, owner, and approval needed. Require every specialist to use the same report format so the coordinator can compare results. Keep a visible queue for blocked tasks and decisions awaiting you. Community users commonly report better results when agents share a common status location and one centralized list of pending decisions. Run My AI Business’s coordination model fits this structure because the owner remains responsible for reviewing drafts and refining instructions.
acceptedAnswer.description: Require a consistent decision brief containing progress, findings, sources, disagreements, assumptions, next action, owner, and approval needed. Maintain one visible queue for blocked work and pending decisions. Judge the system by completed, reviewable outcomes—not by how many assistant messages it produces.
